titulo: Formal style and e-mail: The structure of a formal e-mail

aula.objetivo: Write a formal email with the right subject line, greeting, opening, polite request and sign-off, and switch confidently between the informal register (tú) and the formal one (usted).

sessao.titulo: The structure of a formal e-mail

itens.ru: A la espera de su respuesta
itens.translit: ah lah es-PEH-rah deh soo rres-PWES-tah
itens.audio: A la espera de su respuesta

blocos.titulo: The parts of a formal email
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the subject line says in a few words what the email is about: «Asunto: Solicitud de información». Avoid «Hola» or leaving it blank. STEP 2: the greeting. With a name: «Estimado señor Ruiz:» or «Estimada señora García:». To several people: «Estimados señores:». When you don't know who will read it ("To whom it may concern"): «A quien corresponda:». Spanish puts a colon after the greeting, where English uses a comma; a comma is fine in less formal messages. STEP 3: the opening says why you're writing: «Le escribo para…», «Me dirijo a usted para…», «Me pongo en contacto con ustedes para…». STEP 4: the body: one topic per paragraph, short sentences, and «usted» from start to finish. STEP 5: the closing line before the sign-off: «A la espera de su respuesta,» (Looking forward to your reply), «Quedo a su disposición para cualquier duda.», «Le agradezco de antemano su atención.» (Thank you in advance for your attention.) STEP 6: the sign-off and signature: «Atentamente,» (Yours sincerely), «Un cordial saludo,» (Kind regards), «Cordialmente,», followed by your name. Between friends: «Un abrazo», «Hasta pronto», «Besos». STEP 7: abbreviations: «Sr.» (señor), «Sra.» (señora), «Srta.» (señorita, used less and less). Write them with a full stop. STEP 8: for attachments use «adjunto»: «Adjunto el documento» or «Le envío adjunto el documento».
blocos.comparacao: English "Dear Mr Ruiz" is NOT «Querido señor Ruiz»: «querido» is affectionate, for family and friends. In formal writing use «Estimado». English "Please find attached…" also doesn't translate word for word; the natural Spanish is simply «Adjunto…». And Spanish puts a colon after the greeting: «Estimada señora García:».

tabela.informal: Te escribo para preguntarte una cosa.

erros.motivo: «Querido» is affectionate (like "my dear"); in a formal email use «estimado».

erros.errado: Te escribo para pedir información. (to a company)
Por favor, encuentre adjunto el currículum.
erros.motivo: "Please find attached" is an English formula; Spanish just says «adjunto».

blocos.enunciado: Write, out loud or on paper, the greeting and sign-off of a formal email to a company and then of one to a friend. Note the words that change.
Say out loud the difference between «tú» and «usted» in three sentences: one to a friend, one to a doctor you don't know and one to your boss. Then say five opinion expressions from lesson 53.
